My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is -23.762 degrees and its azimuth is 281.646 degrees, so it is below the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is -51.919 degrees and its azimuth is 275.986 degrees, so it is below the horizon. The Moon is 5.75 percent illuminated, 27.675 degrees from the Sun, and 364757 kilometers away. The sky brightness is night, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

No. The Moon’s center is about **51.9° below the horizon**, so it is geometrically far beneath the Earth from your viewpoint and cannot be seen, regardless of the clear, dark sky or its 5.75% illumination.

At most, atmospheric refraction can shift objects near the horizon by roughly **0.5°**, nowhere near enough to overcome a −51.9° altitude. You would need to wait until the Moon rises; at that time, its thin crescent may be visible if the sky is sufficiently dark and the horizon is unobstructed.
